rules.description: After price briefly trades beyond a recent swing extreme against the trade direction but immediately closes back in the trend direction, enter (or re-enter) on a stop one tick beyond the prior bar's extreme.
rules.pseudocode: stopRunOccurred = low[1] < recentSwingExtreme && close[1] > recentSwingExtreme; enterLongNextOpen = stopRunOccurred && high[0] >= high[1] + entryTick

complexity.reason: needs a tracked recent swing-extreme/stop-cluster level and a breach-then-reclaim detector before the ordinary stop-entry mechanization

rules.merge_notes: Source frames this as 'add to or re-enter' a swing position (multi-unit language), but the mechanism itself -- a breach-and-reclaim of a recent level, entered on a stop -- does not require holding multiple units. Reduces to a single-position Entry (a stop-run continuation entry); mechanized that way, dropping the 'add to an already-open position' framing.

rules.description: When a profit-taking limit exit is filled at exactly the extreme tick of a move (price did not need to trade through the price to fill it), treat this as a sign of unusual trend strength and look to re-enter in the original direction.
rules.pseudocode:
// blocked: needs the fill model to distinguish a touch-only fill from a traded-through fill
exitFilledAtExactExtreme[0]; lookForReentrySameDirection = exitFilledAtExactExtreme[0]

complexity.reason: depends on a fill-model distinction (touched-and-filled vs traded-through) that most backtest fill models, including this one, do not necessarily expose the same way real limit orders behave

rules.merge_notes: Does not reduce to a single-position rule in a way that sidesteps the blocker -- the whole signal IS the fill-quality distinction, not a scaling/multi-unit issue.
design_decisions_needed: limit-order fill model: touch-only vs traded-through fills

rules.description: A meta-gate on every entry: require at least reasonCount independently-true qualifying conditions from an enumerable list of Brooks 'reasons' before allowing the entry.
rules.pseudocode:
// blocked: which sibling Entry filters count as a 'reason' is an authoring-pass design decision
reasonsTrue = countTrue([reasonA[0], reasonB[0], reasonC[0], ...]); allowEntry = reasonsTrue >= reasonCount

complexity.reason: the book's list of 'reasons' mixes filters, patterns, and exits from many other chapters; a design decision is needed to pick and wire the concrete sibling conditions this counts

rules.merge_notes: Keyword-matched to trade_management (the chapter is literally titled 'Need Two Reasons to Take a Trade') but is not a scaling/multi-unit idea; kept here rather than cross-bucketed since no other listed bucket fits a cross-cutting entry-quality meta-gate any better.
design_decisions_needed: enumerable list of entry 'reasons' for TwoReasonsRequiredToEnter

rules.description: Second leg of a scale-in: while a first (half-size) entry is open and unfilled on its own target, place a second buy-limit order a fixed distance below the first entry's fill price to complete the full position.
rules.pseudocode:
// not mechanizable: requires tracking a first, independently-sized unit's fill price while adding a second unit to the same open position
addOnLimitPrice = firstEntryPrice - addOnDistance

complexity.reason: needs the first scaled-in entry's fill price as a reference, on top of its own swing-pivot dependency (R26-14)

rules.merge_notes: Inherently a second unit added to an already-open position -- does not reduce to a single-position rule. Engine's single-position model has no multi-unit tracking; kept as a citation only.

rules.description: During a pullback to a steeply rising moving average, place a buy-limit order a fixed distance below the moving average.
rules.pseudocode: isSteeplyRisingMA = (movingAverage[0] - movingAverage[maSlopeLookback]) / maSlopeLookback >= minMaSlopePerBar; limitPrice = movingAverage[0] - intervalDistance; enterLongOnLimitNextBar = isSteeplyRisingMA && low[1] <= limitPrice

complexity.reason: an MA-slope test plus a single limit price -- mechanizable without the multi-level ladder

rules.merge_notes: Source (ScaleInAtIntervalsBelowRisingMA) describes a ladder of numScaleInLevels buy-limit orders at successive intervals below the MA -- a multi-unit scale-in the engine cannot place as one position. Reduces to a single-position rule at one level (numScaleInLevels=1, i.e. intervalDistance is the offset of the sole limit order); the ladder itself is dropped.

rules.description: While holding a countertrend position, if a second with-trend counting-setup signal (e.g. a High2 while short in a bull trend) fires against it, permit exiting the countertrend position or reversing to the with-trend direction.
rules.pseudocode: isSecondAdverseWithTrendSignal = isHigh2Setup[0] && isBullTrend[0]; allowExitOrReverseToLong = ctx.MarketPosition() == -1 && isSecondAdverseWithTrendSignal

complexity.reason: reuses the H2/L2 counting-setup primitive and a position-state read; the MA-proximity emphasis in the book is a strengthening condition, not a hard requirement

catalog_match.note: Same family as catalog's FlatOrOpenLossExceeds -- an Entry that reads position state to permit a reversal -- but gated on a with-trend counting setup instead of an open-loss threshold.

rules.merge_notes: Reads as a scale-in caveat in the book ('exit or reverse on the second move against a countertrend scale-in') but the rule itself is a single-position permission-to-exit-or-reverse; does not require holding multiple units. Depends on the H2/L2 counting-setup primitive, expected key High2Setup per T10-23/T00-19.

rules.description: Add a further with-trend unit to an already-open long each time the pullback extends to a new low, while the larger trend context is still believed valid.
rules.pseudocode:
// not mechanizable: adds an independently sized/stopped unit to an already-open position
isNewPullbackLow = ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && low[0] < lowest(low, ctx.BarsSinceEntry())[1]

complexity.reason: the engine models one all-or-nothing position; adding independently-tracked units on continued favorable movement is not supported

rules.merge_notes: Explicitly a multi-unit add-to-open-position idea per the source's own notes; kept per the mining brief's instruction to record scaling candidates even though the engine has no multi-unit position model.

rules.description: When adding a second unit at the level where the original stop would have been, widen the protective stop on the entire combined position to roughly twice the original single-unit stop distance, measured from the average entry price.
rules.pseudocode:
// not mechanizable: needs an average entry price across multiple units
averageEntryPrice = weightedAverage(unitEntryPrices, unitSizes); exitLongStop = ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && low[0] <= averageEntryPrice - stopMultiple * originalSingleUnitRiskDollars

complexity.reason: requires an average entry price and a combined stop across multiple units, which the engine's single-position model does not expose

rules.merge_notes: Fundamentally a multi-unit average-entry-price feature; kept as a citation only.

rules.description: Place an additional (or reversal) entry one tick beyond the round-number/obvious stop distance from the original signal, on the premise that a cluster of other traders' stops sits there and the market often runs them before reversing.
rules.pseudocode:
// blocked: 'the obvious stop distance other traders are using' has no formula given
obviousStopDistance = typicalStopDistanceForContext(); scaleInPrice = originalSignalPrice - (obviousStopDistance - tick); allowScaleInShort = high[0] >= scaleInPrice

complexity.reason: the entry arithmetic (one tick beyond a distance) is trivial, but 'the obvious/appropriate stop size for the recent price action' is a discretionary judgment the book does not reduce to a formula

rules.merge_notes: Adding a unit is a multi-unit feature too, but the harder blocker is upstream of that: there is no bar-level definition of 'the obvious stop distance' to test against, so this stays blocked on a design decision even if reduced to a single-position entry.

rules.description: The current bar falls within the first few trading days of the calendar month.

catalog_match.note: DayOfWeekEntry/DayOfWeekAnyOf test weekday, not day-of-month; SeasonalHalfYear tests month, not day; no existing rule tests day-of-month.

rules.merge_notes: Absorbed from the misc bucket (R31-12, DollarCostAverageFixedCalendarInterval): the book cites dollar-cost averaging as a scaling analogy -- buy a fixed FRACTION OF CAPITAL on a fixed calendar schedule regardless of price. The capital-allocation/scheduled-fraction-of-cash part is a portfolio feature the engine's single-position model does not expose and is dropped. The underlying calendar test reduces to a trivial, independently useful Entry filter and is kept atomically.

design_decisions.topic: limit-order fill model: touch-only vs traded-through fills
options: treat any touch (high>=price or low<=price) as a fill, matching the engine's existing fill model, with no distinct 'touched but not through' category
add a distinct touch-only fill category requiring order-book-level detail the engine does not model
design_decisions.recommended: drop -- the engine's fill model doesn't distinguish touch-only fills from trade-through fills, so R24-08's signal isn't observable as stated

design_decisions.topic: enumerable list of entry 'reasons' for TwoReasonsRequiredToEnter
options: hand-pick a fixed list of existing Entry filters (signal-bar quality, MA pullback, breakout pullback, S/R test, counting setup) and count how many are true
rely on the pane system's implicit AND of filters instead of an explicit reason-counter
drop as too vague to mechanize consistently
design_decisions.recommended: drop or defer -- the pane system already ANDs entry filters, so requiring >=2 true filters is close to just placing two filter rules on the same entry; a literal 'reason' counter needs a hand-picked list this bucket can't fix on its own

options: fix it to a small set of round-number distances (e.g. whole points) and test each as an input
derive it from recent realized volatility (e.g. an ATR multiple) as a proxy for 'typical' stop size
drop as discretionary, no bar-level test given
design_decisions.recommended: drop -- the book gives no formula for 'the obvious stop size traders are using'; substituting an ATR proxy would be inventing a new rule, not mechanizing this one

bucket_summary: 9 candidates, all genuinely about position sizing / multi-unit management except R26-01 (a mis-keyworded entry-quality meta-gate, kept here for lack of a better home). Two reduce cleanly to single-position rules once the multi-unit framing is dropped (StopRunReclaimReentry, BuyLimitBelowRisingMA priority A) and one more likewise (CounterSignalReversalPermission, a reversal-permission read of position state). Three are true multi-unit/average-entry-price features the single-position engine cannot express (ScaleInAddOnLimitEntry, ScaleInOnContinuedPullback, WidenCombinedStopToTwiceInitialOnScaleIn) and are graded D. The remaining three are C, each blocked on a real design decision (a fill-model distinction, an undefined 'reason' list, an undefined 'obvious stop size'). Also absorbed R31-12 from the misc bucket as FirstTradingDayOfMonthFilter (its calendar test only; the capital-allocation part is dropped as engine-unsupported). The two strays named in the brief, R28-42 and R29-12, were not present in either bucket file handed to this agent (their primary bucket per secondary.tsv is leg_counting) -- their content was not available here to evaluate for absorption.
